item.title: China improves investment mechanism to advance rural revitalization
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
An aerial drone photo taken on July 29, 2026 shows an agricultural plane carrying out aerial crop protection operations over a farmland of Beidahuang Group in northeast China's Heilongjiang Province. (Photo by Li Ang/Xinhua)
BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- China has unveiled a plan to improve its investment mechanism for rural revitalization as part of broader efforts to boost agricultural and rural development, the country's agriculture ministry said Monday.
Jointly issued by multiple government bodies, including the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, the National Development and Reform Commission and the People's Bank of China, the plan calls for stronger fiscal and financial support and increased social capital participation. The goal is to steadily boost investment in rural revitalization and further optimize the investment structure for agriculture, rural areas and farmers.
By 2030, the country aims to have basically established a rural revitalization investment mechanism aligned with agricultural and rural development conditions, featuring a well-balanced structure, sound approaches and an emphasis on both efficiency and effectiveness, according to the plan.
Emphasizing the leading role of government funding, the plan outlines measures to fully leverage bonds, loans and insurance to support agricultural and rural development, while calling for coordinated efforts by governments, financial institutions and social capital.
Favorable pricing and subsidy policies will also be rolled out in a more coordinated and effective manner, according to the plan.
Addressing issues concerning agriculture, rural areas and farmers remains a top priority on China's development agenda, with advancing rural revitalization across the board serving as a key task.
To this end, the outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) stresses improving the effectiveness of policies aimed at strengthening agriculture, benefiting farmers and enriching rural areas. It calls for improving related mechanisms and policy frameworks, facilitating the two-way flow of resources between urban and rural areas, and injecting greater vitality into agricultural and rural development.

item.title: China to reinvent centuries-old industries with heritage and AI
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- China on Monday unveiled its first national policy document for silk, tea, porcelain and other centuries-old industries, as part of efforts to leverage the country's rich cultural heritage and build strong global brands.
By 2028, the country aims to cultivate 50 enterprises with annual revenues exceeding 10 billion yuan (about 1.48 billion U.S. dollars) each, Xie Yuansheng, vice minister of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), told a news conference.
The document also calls for 100 Chinese consumer brands and several industrial clusters with annual output exceeding 100 billion yuan to be developed by 2028, he added.
By 2030, these industries are expected to produce a group of world-class enterprises and renowned brands, while moving toward the mid- to high-end of the global value chain, according to the document issued by the MIIT and five other government departments.
In addition to the industries mentioned above, the document also covers traditional Chinese medicine, brewing, arts and crafts, and the "four treasures of the study" -- writing brush, ink stick, paper and inkstone -- all deeply rooted in Chinese culture and traditions dating back centuries or even millennia.
Representative sectors of these traditional industries boast about 25,000 enterprises above the designated size, employing nearly 3.5 million people and generating about 8 trillion yuan in annual revenue, according to Xie.
Historically, these products traveled along ancient trade routes as far as Central Asia, the Mediterranean and even Africa, carrying Chinese craftsmanship and culture far beyond the country's borders.
In recent years, the appeal of Chinese culture overseas has continued to rise. Content creators around the world are making aspects of Chinese culture part of their daily lives -- from drinking hot water and wearing slippers around the house to eating Chinese food and wearing red.
The document also comes as China seeks to translate its rich cultural heritage into greater market competitiveness.
About 90 percent of China's silk products are exported, but mainly as raw materials or original equipment manufacturer goods, with domestic brands having limited pricing power in the global market, said Feng Haicang, an official with the MIIT's consumer goods industry department.
"Our challenge is to make sure these time-honored crafts are not only admired but also commercially successful, and to restore these historic Chinese products to their rightful place at the high end of international markets," said Feng.
China will hold the first national exposition of time-honored industries in east China's Hangzhou City in late October, Xie said.
AI is expected to play an important part in boosting these industries, according to the document. The technology will be used to digitize traditional craft knowledge, decode traditional production processes and improve efficiency and product quality on factory floors.
In silk weaving, AI-assisted design can now generate thousands of patterns in minutes, said Xie.
A DEEP POOL OF CRAFT KNOWLEDGE
These industries draw strength from China's vast intangible cultural heritage, which provides a deep reservoir of craft knowledge, skills and cultural creativity for their continued development, said Shan Gangxin, an official with the Ministry of Culture and Tourism, at the news conference.
Traditional arts, crafts and medicine, Shan noted, share deep roots with industries like silk, tea and porcelain, and have evolved alongside them.
China now has 45 elements inscribed on UNESCO's lists and register of intangible cultural heritage, including silk craftsmanship, acupuncture and tea-processing techniques. More than 100,000 items are also recognized on national, provincial, prefectural and county-level intangible cultural heritage lists.
In July, the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites were added to the UNESCO World Heritage List.
The country's large pool of skilled practitioners is also a solid base for industrial development. More than 200 universities have taken part in training programs for intangible cultural heritage practitioners over the past decade, benefiting more than 200,000 heritage inheritors, said Shan.
The economic potential of traditional skills is already clear in the way they have been adapted to today's markets.
Willow weaving in Linyi, east China's Shandong Province, for example, has evolved from a craft once best known for making baskets and hampers into a wide range of contemporary products, from stylish cultural and creative products to playful items such as cat climbing frames.
The industry now has more than 300 patents and over 20,000 product designs, with its products reaching more than 80 countries and regions, according to Shan.
Traditional craftsmanship is also finding new channels and audiences. This summer, creative products featuring hemp weaving, Huzhou writing brushes and Zhuang brocade were officially licensed for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
By the end of 2025, China had 14,900 intangible cultural heritage workshops, supporting employment and higher incomes for more than 1.3 million people, Shan said.

item.title: China's major river-to-sea canal to open to navigation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
An aerial drone photo taken on Aug. 12, 2026 shows a trial vessel driving past a bridge for animals over the Pinglu Canal in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. (Xinhua/Zhou Hua)
NANNING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- Pinglu Canal in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region will become operational on Sept. 16, according to a Monday press conference on the canal's opening.
The 134.2-km canal links the Xijiang River shipping route in the north with the Beibu Gulf in the south. It is China's first major river-to-sea canal project that has been planned and coordinated at the national level since 1949.
Designed to accommodate vessels of up to 5,000 tonnes, the canal stretches along the country's New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, a strategic route linking China's inland regions with ASEAN and other global markets.
It is expected to shorten the shipping distance between China's southwestern hinterland and ASEAN by 560 km and reduce logistics costs by 18 to 30 percent, said Lu Xinning, vice chairperson of the regional government, in another press conference held in early September.
"The canal not only overcomes Guangxi's longstanding constraints on river-to-sea connectivity, but will also reshape the economic geography between China and ASEAN," said Lu.
Trade between the two sides has seen robust growth in recent years. Data from General Administration of Customs show that bilateral trade between China and ASEAN reached 4.34 trillion yuan (about 640 billion U.S. dollars) in the first half of 2026, up 18.2 percent year on year.
The Beibu Gulf Port, a key hub at the southern end of the canal, has become an important gateway for China's opening up to ASEAN. Its container throughput increased from 2.28 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU) in 2017 to 10.06 million TEUs in 2025, and the port has established a comprehensive shipping network that covers major ports across ASEAN.

item.title: International journalists witness China's rescue efforts in mudslide-ravaged Gyirong
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
* A group of journalists from international media outlets, including CNN, Reuters and NBC, visited the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region from Saturday to Sunday. The fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, struck Gyirong Port on Aug. 26. As of 6 p.m. on Sept. 5, 43 people were confirmed dead and 519 remained missing.
* At a media briefing by the local emergency rescue headquarters, the journalists heard from technical experts and local officials about ongoing efforts on multiple fronts: the search for the missing, victim identification, community assistance and secondary disaster prevention.
* "It's a very difficult condition for the workers, and I very much admired how they keep searching for people," said Brazilian journalist Bruno Falci Bitarelli Medeiros, noting that as global warming is the root cause of the disaster, more concrete actions from the world are needed to prevent these kinds of disasters from happening again.
GYIRONG, Xizang, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- Even with prior knowledge of the catastrophe, Brazilian journalist Bruno Falci Bitarelli Medeiros was struck by the harsh rescue conditions after a bumpy 12-hour bus ride from Lhasa to the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region.
The final stretch wound through rugged mountain roads, unpredictable weather and falling rocks. "It's a very difficult condition for the workers, and I very much admired how they keep searching for people," Medeiros said.
Medeiros was among a group of journalists from international media outlets including CNN, Reuters and NBC who visited the devastated port from Saturday to Sunday.
A press conference attended by domestic and foreign journalists is held in Gyirong County, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, Sept. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Tenzin Nyida)
At a media briefing by the local emergency rescue headquarters, they heard from technical experts and local officials about ongoing efforts on multiple fronts: the search for the missing, victim identification, community assistance and secondary disaster prevention.
The fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, struck Gyirong Port in Xigaze City on the China-Nepal border on Aug. 26. As of 6 p.m. on Sept. 5, 43 people were confirmed dead and 519 remained missing.
SEARCH GOING ON
At the core disaster zone, a 35-meter-high flood mark, roughly the height of a 12-story building, was scored into the cliff above the ruins.
"Everything below the flood mark was originally underwater," said Norbu Tsering, deputy head of the emergency rescue headquarters and acting mayor of Xigaze City. "Power was gone. What you see now is what we've restored in the past couple of days."
Rescuers conduct search and rescue operations at the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, Sept. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Tenzin Nyida)
Land access to the port was restored on the morning of Sept. 2, allowing heavy machinery to move in and clear working areas.
Mud deposits average four meters deep in the hardest-hit zone, with some areas reaching 16 meters. Inside the core area, vehicles and machinery are conducting deep-search operations -- excavating, searching and clearing layer by layer during grid-by-grid sweeps.
Konda Jagan Mohan Varma from the Press Trust of India watched the operation. "The glacier breakdown brought down a lot of slush, mud and huge rocks together," he said. "A large part of infrastructure was damaged on both sides, in China and Nepal."
He noted the scale of the rescue effort unfolding around him -- heavy machinery carving through the debris, teams fanning out across the ruins in methodical searches.
Just an hour after the journalists arrived, the valley turned from sunshine to pounding rain, forcing an emergency evacuation. Rescuers have persisted in such conditions for more than 10 days.
As of 6 p.m. on Sept. 5, China had deployed over 2,500 rescue personnel, more than 500 vehicle trips and over 9,000 sets of search equipment, and air-dropped more than 5 tonnes of supplies. Two people from a nearby village have been rescued, and nearly 1,000 personal items have been recovered.
BEYOND BORDERS
After repeated verification, authorities confirmed that 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries, including Nepal, India, Latvia, the United States and Britain, remain missing.
For identification, each body is numbered, photographed and sampled for DNA and dental records at the scene. The headquarters has set up a dedicated identification team. So far, none of the bodies retrieved are foreign nationals.
Rescuers work at the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, Sept. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Tenzin Nyida)
Responding to a question about the identification process for the missing, Yang Lahong, deputy director of the foreign affairs office of Xizang, said at the briefing that the names and specific information of missing foreigners have not been made public to protect their privacy, but have been shared with the relevant embassies through diplomatic channels.
A 24-hour hotline for families of missing foreign nationals has received 509 calls, with feedback provided promptly, Yang added.
At Nepal's request, the Chinese government has dispatched tunnel rescue and DNA testing experts to Nepal, along with emergency material assistance. Through a China-Nepal disaster prevention information notification mechanism, daily updates on meteorology, hydrology, glacial lakes and glaciers are shared with Nepal.
After the disaster, many Nepalese border residents were stranded in China due to the port closure. Local authorities have seen to the daily needs of 1,720 Nepalese border residents.
Green channels for foreign personnel entry and exit have been opened. A total of 3,388 foreign nationals originally planning to leave via Gyirong Port have been diverted, and authorities have helped 365 Nepalese border residents cross the border to return home.
WATCHING FOR NEXT DANGER
Preventing secondary disasters remains a priority. More than 170 experts and technicians are now monitoring the area with over 150 sets of equipment, including slope radar and drones.
Along the main rescue route, 58 geological hazard spots have been identified, seven of them high-risk.
Rescuers use a laser-based AI monitoring device to dynamically monitor risks such as landslides and falling rocks at the mudslide-hit area in Gyirong County, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, Aug. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Jigme Dorje)
Hu Bo, leader of the China Anneng rescue detection team, serves as a "sentinel" for frontline workers. When upstream data showed abnormal movement, he sounded the retreat signal. Whistles echoed through the gorge as personnel and machinery pulled back to safety zones.
Hu said such scenarios can happen several times a night.
Muhammad Asghar from the Associated Press of Pakistan observed the monitoring efforts. "The monitoring for secondary disasters is being done tirelessly, day and night," he said.
On the site, Medeiros spotted civilian drones flying to observe potential risks for a secondary disaster.
"The technology today is being very helpful to rescue operations in this disaster," he said. "Some countries use drones for war, but China uses drones to help people."
Medeiros noted that, as global warming is the root cause of the disaster, more concrete actions from the world are needed to prevent these kinds of disasters from happening again, citing China's push for a green economy as an example.
Asghar agreed. "Climate change is not the issue of only one country. The whole world should put their heads together," he said.

item.title: AI to take center stage at 5th global digital expo
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
People visit the 4th Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province, Sept. 25, 2025. (Xinhua/Jiang Han)
BEIJING, Sept. 8 (Xinhua) -- The 5th Global Digital Trade Expo, an event dedicated to promoting digital trade and industrial cooperation, will take place from Sept. 23 to 27 in Hangzhou, capital of east China's Zhejiang Province, with artificial intelligence (AI) as its main theme, an official said on Monday.
More than one-third of the exhibitors will focus on AI, alongside the collective debut of AI application pilot bases, presenting a full-chain innovation ecosystem spanning foundational models, industry applications and smart devices, China's Vice Minister of Commerce Yan Dong noted.
A number of AI competitions will be held on the sidelines of the expo, covering areas such as open-source development, embodied intelligence and brain-computer interface technology.
The expo will feature 170,000 square meters of exhibition space, with international exhibitors accounting for over 20 percent of the total. The number of overseas pavilions has already exceeded the combined total of all previous editions.
Malaysia and Hungary will be the guest countries of honor, while representatives from 121 countries and regions and 29 international organizations have confirmed their attendance.
The expo has so far attracted nearly 40,000 professional buyers, including more than 12,000 from overseas, with expected international procurement orders reaching 977 million U.S. dollars.
China's digitally deliverable service trade value expanded at an average annual rate of 11.2 percent between 2016 and 2025, outpacing the global average by 1.8 percentage points.
According to a guideline on boosting reform and innovative development of digital trade released in November 2024, China expects the share of digitally deliverable service trade in total service trade to exceed 45 percent by 2029 and 50 percent by 2035.
The Ministry of Commerce will work with other government departments to implement the guideline, support local governments in tailoring policies to boost digital trade, and foster a coordinated effort to advance the sector, Yan added.

item.title: Book introducing Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization published
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
BEIJING, Sept. 7 (Xinhua) -- A book introducing Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization has been published by the Higher Education Press and the People's Publishing House.
Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC) in 2012, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has approached ecological conservation from the perspective of ensuring the sustainable development of the Chinese nation.
With a profound understanding of the important position and strategic significance of ecological conservation in the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics for a new era, the CPC Central Committee has vigorously advanced theoretical, practical and institutional innovation in this field, put forward a series of new ideas, new thinking and new strategies, led historic, transformative and comprehensive changes in China's ecological conservation, and developed Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization.
The book introducing the thought, compiled under the organization of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee and the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, consists of an introduction and nine chapters, totaling about 170,000 Chinese characters.
It systematically expounds on the significance, theoretical framework, essence, connotations and practical requirements of Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization.

item.title: Xi extends congratulations on 70th anniversary of China Media Group's Xiaolaba program for children
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-07
BEIJING, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, sent a congratulatory letter on Sept. 4 to a popular children's program of China Media Group named Xiaolaba, or Little Trumpet, on the 70th anniversary of the program's premiere.
In his letter, Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, expressed his appreciation for the program's persistent commitment to "telling good stories to children" and accompanying generations of youngsters for their healthy growth over the past 70 years.
Xi emphasized that from this new starting point, the staff of the program as well as the broad ranks of children's literary and art professionals are expected to deliver on the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education, keep pace with the pulse of the times, cultivate the fertile soil of children's culture, and dedicate the mind and passion to creating more excellent works that promote truth, goodness and beauty and are beloved by children.
Xi urged the team and related professionals to make greater contributions to nurturing new generations of capable youngsters who can help build up and carry on the socialist cause with well-rounded development in terms of moral grounding, intellectual ability, physical vigor, aesthetic sensibility and work skills.
Premiered on Sept. 4, 1956, Xiaolaba is the first radio broadcast program of New China fully dedicated to preschool children. It has now developed into a famed brand that integrates radio, television, new media, and on-campus broadcasting.

item.title: Rescuers repair critical road section to mudslide-hit border port in Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
Rescuers on Saturday restored the first sharp-curve section on the national highway G216 -- where the roadbed had been completely destroyed -- preparing for full reopening of this critical lifeline to the mudslide-hit border port of Gyirong in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region.

item.title: Pushing in by Land, Water and Air: Expert Explains Extreme Hurdles in Mudslide Rescue
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
A total of 2,141 rescue personnel have been mobilized for search and rescue operations after a mudslide struck Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. Rescue teams are advancing into the hardest-hit core area simultaneously by water, land and air. An expert explained mudslides like this occur under particular terrain and water conditions, and that creates several challenges for rescue teams.
